PREFACE Since  the  days  of  Nissor  Singh  no  one  has  made  an  attempt to  compile  a Kbasi-Khasi  Dictionary.  If  there  has  been  a silent  attempt  by  any  silent  worker  such  work  has  not seen  the  light  of  the  day.  But  U larington  Kharkongngor has  revived  the  interest  in  enriching  the  Khasi  vocabulary by  compiling  a Khasi-Khasi  Dictionary  which  he  entitles “Ka  Dienshonhi.”  I hope  this  work  of  U larington  Khar* kongngor  will  stand  as  a pioneering  work  in  this  hne  for  the present  and  future  generations.  For  the  last  four  or  live  years I have  watched  the  great  enthusiasm  that  Mr.  Kharkongngor has  taken  in  the  field  of  Khasi  literature,  with  great  interest. As  a student  of  this  subject  he  has  shown  his  capacity  that he  has  got  a strong  command  of  the  Khasi  language  and  a mastery  over  its  vocabulary.  This  work  is  an  embodiment of  that  command  and  mastery  over  the  Khasi  language  that this  young  man  has  brought  out  to  light.  I have  the  privilege of  having  been  his  teacher  as  well  as  in  reading  the  manus- cript very  thoroughly  and  1 have  a great  hope  that  this  work will  render  great  benefits  upon  the  general  public  and  the  elite of  the  Khasi  society  as  well.  I have  a great  hope  that  this

young  man  will  rise  very  high  in  life  as  an  author. Prof.  R.  S.  LYNGDOH,  M.A., Head  of  the  Department  of  Khasi, St.  Anthony’s  College,  Shillong. FOREWORD Mr.  laringtoti  Kharkongngor  has  taken  great  pains to  write  this  Khasi-to*Khasi  dictionary.  It  is  a pioneering work  of  very  great  importance  in  the  development  of  the Khasi  language  and  of  Khasi  literature. The  book  is  by  no  means  perfect.  While  there  will  be a great  number  of  Khasi  literati  who  will  not  agree  with  the introduction,  in  this  book,  of  some  words  into  the  Khasi language  or  with  the  meaning  given  tu  some  others,  the book,  I am  sure,  will  not  only  meet  the  need  of  those  who may  not  be  very  familiar  with  the  Khasi  language  and  who wish  to  enrich  their  knowledge  of  it,  but  it  will  also  contri- bute greatly  to  the  growth  of  the  Khasi  language.  Many Khasi  words  which  are  dying  because  of  the  onslaught  of other  more  powerful  languages  such  as  English  and  Hindi will,  as  the  result  of  this  effort  on  the  part  of  Mr.  larington Kharkongngor,  come  back  to  life.  This  work  may  even enrich  the  languages  of  other  racial  groups,  our  neighbours in  the  State  of  Assam. In  going  through  the  pages  of  this  book  in  the  manus- cript form,  I have  tried  to  indicate  in  several  places  where  f

question  the  correctness  of  his  statements  or  of  the  words used;  but  as  the  book  is  entirely  the  result  of  his  painstaking labour,  I have  tried  to  avoid  as  far  as  possible  any  imposition of  my  viewpoint  on  what  the  author  himself  considers  to be  the  correct  word,  correct  statement,  correct  spelling  or correct  punctuation. I am,  however,  happy  that  the  author  gave  me  this honour  and  privilege  to  go  through  the  manuscript.  As  the result  of  this  opportunity  there  has  grown  in  me  a feeling of  appreciation  and  respect  for  the  good  work  which  Mr. vn larington  Kharkongngor  as  a young  man  has  been  able  to do  for  his  own  people,  the  Khasis. If  there  has  been  a silent  attempt  by  any  silent  worker  such  work  has  not seen  the  light  of  the  day. For  the  last  four  or  live  years I have  watched  the  great  enthusiasm  that  Mr.  Kharkongngor has  taken  in  the  field  of  Khasi  literature,  with  great  interest. This  work  is  an  embodiment of  that  command  and  mastery  over  the  Khasi  language  that this  young  man  has  brought  out  to  light.  I have  the  privilege of  having  been  his  teacher  as  well  as  in  reading  the  manus- cript very  thoroughly  and  1 have  a great  hope  that  this  work will  render  great  benefits  upon  the  general  public  and  the  elite of  the  Khasi  society  as  well. FOREWORD Mr.  laringtoti  Kharkongngor  has  taken  great  pains to  write  this  Khasi-to*Khasi  dictionary.  It  is  a pioneering work  of  very  great  importance  in  the  development  of  the Khasi  language  and  of  Khasi  literature. The  book  is  by  no  means  perfect.  While  there  will  be a great  number  of  Khasi  literati  who  will  not  agree  with  the introduction,  in  this  book,  of  some  words  into  the  Khasi language  or  with  the  meaning  given  tu  some  others,  the book,  I am  sure,  will  not  only  meet  the  need  of  those  who may  not  be  very  familiar  with  the  Khasi  language  and  who wish  to  enrich  their  knowledge  of  it,  but  it  will  also  contri- bute greatly  to  the  growth  of  the  Khasi  language.  Many Khasi  words  which  are  dying  because  of  the  onslaught  of other  more  powerful  languages  such  as  English  and  Hindi will,  as  the  result  of  this  effort  on  the  part  of  Mr.  larington Kharkongngor,  come  back  to  life.  This  work  may  even enrich  the  languages  of  other  racial  groups,  our  neighbours in  the  State  of  Assam.
